107	    invisible by the time a tool function runs in the SDK's own task.

109	    Whenever ``ctx.request`` is present (HTTP/SSE) this middleware is
110	    **authoritative** for the request: it always calls ``current_role.set(...)``
111	    with the scope's role or ``None``, never leaving the prior value in place.
112	    This matters because asyncio tasks copy their context from whichever task
113	    *spawned* them, not from the ASGI task that stashed the scope value — a
114	    per-request dispatch task can in principle inherit a non-``None``
115	    :data:`current_role` from a long-lived parent task's context. Always
116	    setting (instead of only setting when a role is present) means a request
117	    that carries no role can never observe a stale value some earlier
118	    request's task left behind; it deterministically resolves to the static
119	    default via :func:`resolve_role`, exactly like the old
120	    ``_role_from_request`` mechanism this middleware replaces.
121	
122	    A true no-op only on stdio (``ctx.request`` is ``None`` there — there is
123	    no per-message scope to read, so :data:`current_role` is left untouched
124	    for stdio's own, non-HTTP path).

127	    async def __call__(
128	        self,
129	        ctx: ServerRequestContext[object, object],
130	        call_next: CallNext,
131	    ) -> HandlerResult:
132	        request = getattr(ctx, "request", None)
133	        if request is None:
134	            return await call_next(ctx)
135	        scope = getattr(request, "scope", None)
136	        raw_role = scope.get(_ROLE_SCOPE_KEY) if isinstance(scope, dict) else None
137	        role = raw_role if isinstance(raw_role, str) else None
138	        token = current_role.set(role)
139	        try:
140	            return await call_next(ctx)
141	        finally:
142	            current_role.reset(token)

153	class TenantSqlDriver(SqlDriver):
154	    """``SqlDriver`` subclass that prepends ``SET LOCAL ROLE`` to every txn.
155	
156	    The vendored driver opens a fresh transaction per query (explicit
157	    ``BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY`` for read-only, implicit per-statement
158	    for writes). To make ``SET LOCAL ROLE`` valid for write paths too,
159	    we wrap every execution in an explicit transaction.
160	
161	    When :func:`resolve_role` returns ``None``, the override path is
162	    skipped and the call falls back to the upstream method unchanged
163	    — keeping the cost at exactly one ContextVar lookup per query
164	    when tenancy isn't configured.
165	    """
166	
167	    def __init__(self, *args: Any, default_role: str | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
168	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
169	        self._default_role = default_role
170	
171	    async def _execute_with_connection(  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
172	        self,
173	        connection,
174	        query,
175	        params,
176	        force_readonly,
177	    ):
178	        role = resolve_role(self._default_role)
179	        if role is None:
180	            return await super()._execute_with_connection(connection, query, params, force_readonly)
181	        return await _execute_with_role(connection, query, params, force_readonly, role)
182	
183	
184	async def _execute_with_role(
185	    connection: Any,
186	    query: str,
187	    params: Any,
188	    force_readonly: bool,
189	    role: str,
190	) -> Any:
191	    """Run ``query`` inside an explicit transaction with ``SET LOCAL ROLE``.
192	
193	    Mirrors the upstream :meth:`SqlDriver._execute_with_connection`
194	    flow (begin → execute → fetch / commit / rollback) but always
195	    opens an explicit transaction so ``SET LOCAL`` is valid even on
196	    write paths, and resets the role on every exit branch.
197	    """
198	    # Defence-in-depth — role is already validated at config / middleware,
199	    # but a misconfigured caller could still pass an unvalidated string.
200	    validate_role(role)
201	    transaction_started = False
202	    try:
203	        async with connection.cursor(row_factory=dict_row) as cursor:
204	            if force_readonly:
205	                await cursor.execute("BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY")
206	            else:
207	                await cursor.execute("BEGIN")
208	            transaction_started = True
209	
210	            await cursor.execute(f'SET LOCAL ROLE "{role}"')
211	
212	            if params:
213	                await cursor.execute(query, params)
214	            else:
215	                await cursor.execute(query)
216	
217	            while cursor.nextset():
218	                pass
219	
220	            if cursor.description is None:
221	                # No result set — DDL / DML without RETURNING.
222	                if force_readonly:
223	                    await cursor.execute("ROLLBACK")
224	                else:
225	                    await cursor.execute("COMMIT")
226	                transaction_started = False
227	                return None
228	
229	            rows = await cursor.fetchall()
230	            if force_readonly:
231	                await cursor.execute("ROLLBACK")
232	            else:
233	                await cursor.execute("COMMIT")
234	            transaction_started = False
235	            return [SqlDriver.RowResult(cells=dict(row)) for row in rows]
236	    except BaseException:
237	        if transaction_started:
238	            try:
239	                await connection.rollback()
240	            except asyncio.CancelledError:
241	                # Re-raise cancellation so the caller's cancel scope
242	                # actually unwinds; never swallow it inside a fallback.
243	                raise
244	            except Exception as rollback_error:
245	                logger.error("Error rolling back transaction during role-wrapped execute: %s", rollback_error)
246	        raise

41	class AuditedMCPServer(MCPServer[AppContext]):
42	    """An MCPServer that records an audit event for every tool call."""

44	    rate_limiter: RateLimiter

52	    def _log_if_slow(self, name: str, duration: float) -> None:
53	        if not hasattr(self, "mcpg_settings"):
54	            return
55	        threshold_ms = self.mcpg_settings.slow_call_threshold_ms
56	        if threshold_ms <= 0:
57	            return

59	        if duration > threshold_sec:
60	            import logging
61	
62	            logger = logging.getLogger("mcpg.server")
63	            logger.warning(
64	                "Slow tool call: %s took %.3fs (threshold: %.3fs)",
65	                name,
66	                duration,
67	                threshold_sec,
68	            )

70	    async def call_tool(
71	        self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any], context: Context[AppContext, Any] | None = None
72	    ) -> CallToolResult | InputRequiredResult:
73	        self.in_flight_calls += 1
74	        try:
75	            # Enforce rate limiting if configured

77	                allowed = await self.rate_limiter.consume(name)
78	                if not allowed:
79	                    raise RuntimeError(f"Rate limit exceeded for tool {name!r}. Please try again later.")
80	
81	            metrics = get_metrics()
82	            # Resolve the capability bucket once per call so both the
83	            # OTel span attribute and the Prometheus counter carry the
84	            # same label. `classify_tool` returns None for tools that
85	            # don't match any override / pattern — defensively use
86	            # "unknown" so the label dimension stays cardinality-stable.
87	            bucket = about.classify_tool(name) or "unknown"
88	            start = time.monotonic()
89	            try:
90	                with tool_span(self.otel_tracer, name, arguments, bucket=bucket):
91	                    result = await super().call_tool(name, arguments, context)
92	            except Exception as exc:
93	                duration = time.monotonic() - start
94	                self._log_if_slow(name, duration)
95	                audit.record(audit.AuditEvent(tool=name, arguments=arguments, status="error", error=str(exc)))
96	                metrics.record_call(name, "error", duration, bucket=bucket)
97	                raise
98	            duration = time.monotonic() - start
99	            self._log_if_slow(name, duration)
100	            audit.record(audit.AuditEvent(tool=name, arguments=arguments, status="ok"))
101	            metrics.record_call(name, "ok", duration, bucket=bucket)

107	def make_lifespan(
108	    settings: Settings,
109	    database: Database,
110	    listen_manager: ListenManager,
111	    cursor_manager: CursorManager,
112	    analytical_runner: AnalyticalRunner | None = None,
113	) -> Callable[[MCPServer[AppContext]], AbstractAsyncContextManager[AppContext]]:
114	    """Build the server lifespan: open the database on start, close on stop.
115	
116	    The listen manager is created eagerly (cheap — it doesn't open the
117	    listener connection until the first ``subscribe_channel`` call) and
118	    torn down on lifespan exit so subscriptions can't outlive the
119	    server. The cursor manager holds dedicated connections per open
120	    server-side cursor and is closed-out symmetrically.
121	    """
122	
123	    @asynccontextmanager
124	    async def lifespan(_server: MCPServer[AppContext]) -> AsyncIterator[AppContext]:
125	        from mcpg.cache import CacheManager, cache_namespace
126	
127	        cache_manager = CacheManager(
128	            enabled=settings.cache_enabled,
129	            ttl_seconds=settings.cache_ttl_seconds,
130	            maxsize=settings.cache_maxsize,
131	            redis_url=settings.redis_url,
132	            namespace=cache_namespace(settings.database_url),
133	        )
134	        await cache_manager.start()
135	        if analytical_runner is not None:
136	            await analytical_runner.start()
137	        try:
138	            async with database, listen_manager, cursor_manager:
139	                yield AppContext(
140	                    settings=settings,
141	                    database=database,
142	                    listen_manager=listen_manager,
143	                    cursor_manager=cursor_manager,
144	                    cache=cache_manager,
145	                    analytical_runner=analytical_runner,
146	                )
147	        finally:
148	            if analytical_runner is not None:
149	                await analytical_runner.close()
150	            if hasattr(_server, "in_flight_calls"):
151	                import asyncio
152	                import logging
153	
154	                logger = logging.getLogger("mcpg.server")
155	
156	                drain_start = time.monotonic()
157	                drain_timeout = settings.shutdown_drain_seconds
158	
159	                while _server.in_flight_calls > 0:
160	                    elapsed = time.monotonic() - drain_start
161	                    if elapsed >= drain_timeout:
162	                        logger.warning(
163	                            "Shutdown drain timed out after %ds; force exiting with %d tool calls in-flight",
164	                            drain_timeout,
165	                            _server.in_flight_calls,
166	                        )
167	                        break
168	                    logger.info("Waiting for %d in-flight tool calls to drain...", _server.in_flight_calls)
169	                    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
170	
171	            await cache_manager.close()
172	
173	            # Flush pending OTel spans so a clean shutdown doesn't
174	            # drop the last batch of traces. Tracer is process-wide
175	            # global but the provider hung off the server lets us
176	            # invoke shutdown only when we actually own it.
177	            if hasattr(_server, "otel_tracer") and _server.otel_tracer is not None:
178	                _server.otel_tracer.shutdown()
179	
180	    return lifespan

333	class _IPAllowlistMiddleware:
334	    """ASGI middleware that rejects clients whose IP isn't on the allowlist.
335	
336	    The allowlist is a tuple of IP-address or CIDR-range strings. Each
337	    entry is pre-parsed into an ``ipaddress`` network at construction
338	    time so the request-time check is just a membership test.
339	
340	    The matching IP is the **immediate** connecting peer
341	    (``scope["client"][0]``). ``X-Forwarded-For`` is deliberately
342	    *not* honoured: trusting a forwarded header without a verified
343	    upstream is a well-known spoofing vector, and operators behind a
344	    reverse proxy already terminate TLS there and can enforce the
345	    allowlist at that layer (where it composes with the proxy's own
346	    auditing).
347	
348	    Failure mode is a minimal 403 — no header echo, no body specifics
349	    — so a scanning attacker can't fingerprint the allowlist from the
350	    response.
351	    """
352	
353	    def __init__(self, app: object, *, allowlist: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
354	        import ipaddress
355	
356	        self._app = app
357	        # Pre-parse once at construction. ``strict=False`` makes
358	        # single addresses like ``1.2.3.4`` valid networks (their
359	        # /32 or /128 sibling), so membership testing is uniform
360	        # across single-IP and CIDR entries.
361	        self._networks: tuple[ipaddress.IPv4Network | ipaddress.IPv6Network, ...] = tuple(
362	            ipaddress.ip_network(entry, strict=False) for entry in allowlist
363	        )
364	
365	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
366	        if scope["type"] != "http":
367	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
368	            return
369	
370	        if not self._client_is_allowed(scope):
371	            await _send_403(send, "ip not on allowlist")
372	            return
373	
374	        await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
375	
376	    def _client_is_allowed(self, scope: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
377	        import ipaddress
378	
379	        client = scope.get("client")
380	        # ASGI spec says ``client`` is a two-item iterable ``[host, port]``
381	        # — most servers hand it back as a tuple, some hand back a list,
382	        # so accept both. A missing entry can't be matched against any
383	        # allowlist; deny so a bug in a transport layer can't accidentally
384	        # turn the gate off.
385	        if not isinstance(client, (list, tuple)) or not client:
386	            return False
387	        try:
388	            peer = ipaddress.ip_address(str(client[0]))
389	        except ValueError:
390	            return False
391	        return any(peer in network for network in self._networks)

482	class _RequestTimeoutMiddleware:
483	    """ASGI middleware that caps wall-clock time for a single request.
484	
485	    Off by default (``MCPG_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0``); only
486	    installed when a positive timeout is configured. Intended for
487	    request/response deployments — note that a hard cap will also cut
488	    off long-lived streaming responses, so leave it disabled if you
489	    rely on long SSE / streamable-http streams.
490	
491	    On expiry, if the downstream app has not started the response yet,
492	    a 504 is emitted; if bytes were already sent we can only abort the
493	    stream (the status line is long gone).
494	    """
495	
496	    def __init__(self, app: object, *, timeout_seconds: int) -> None:
497	        self._app = app
498	        self._timeout = timeout_seconds
499	
500	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
501	        if scope["type"] != "http":
502	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
503	            return
504	
505	        started = False
506	
507	        async def send_wrapper(message: dict[str, object]) -> None:
508	            nonlocal started
509	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
510	                started = True
511	            await send(message)  # type: ignore[operator]
512	
513	        try:
514	            async with asyncio.timeout(self._timeout):
515	                await self._app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)  # type: ignore[operator]

519	            # ruff UP041 rejects it), so they can't be distinguished
520	            # at catch time. If an inner app ever raises a bare
521	            # ``TimeoutError`` we'd mis-attribute it to our cap; this
522	            # is preferable to leaking an exception out of the
523	            # middleware. Inner apps that want to surface their own
524	            # timeout should raise a domain-specific subclass.
525	            # Only safe to write a status line if the app hasn't already.
526	            if not started:
527	                await _send_504(send, f"request exceeded {self._timeout}s")

533	    Args:

541	        everything except the exempt paths.

546	    # ``sse_app`` only accept a ``host`` kwarg — NOT ``port`` — despite the
547	    # migration plan's assumption that ``streamable_http_app`` took both
548	    # (verified via ``inspect.signature`` against
549	    # ``mcp.server.mcpserver.server.MCPServer`` before writing this; see
550	    # task-4-report.md). ``host`` alone drives whether the SDK auto-enables
551	    # DNS-rebinding protection scoped to localhost (``sse_app``/
552	    # ``streamable_http_app`` treat ``127.0.0.1``/``localhost``/``::1``
553	    # specially) — passing the configured host, rather than relying on the
554	    # SDK's ``"127.0.0.1"`` default, is what actually fixes the regression:
555	    # without it, binding to e.g. ``0.0.0.0`` would still get the
556	    # localhost-only transport-security defaults baked in.

558	        app = server.streamable_http_app(host=settings.http_host)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

632	    # without hiding real type errors.
633	    from typing import cast as _cast

643	    terminates TLS itself. Adding ``http_tls_ca_certs`` and
644	    flipping ``http_tls_client_cert_required=true`` upgrades the
645	    listener to full mutual TLS — connections without a client cert
646	    signed by a CA in the bundle are refused at the handshake
647	    layer, before any ASGI middleware sees the request.

656	    # needs a SelectorEventLoop. ``__main__`` sets the selector policy at
657	    # startup, but uvicorn's own loop setup reinstalls the *proactor*
658	    # policy on Windows before serving — which silently breaks every
659	    # database connection under the HTTP transport (the connection pool
660	    # times out after 30s and the session crashes). stdio is unaffected;
661	    # nothing overrides the policy there. Re-pin the selector policy and
662	    # tell uvicorn to leave the loop alone (``loop="none"``) so it runs on
663	    # the loop our policy creates. No-op off Windows.
664	    if sys.platform == "win32":
665	        # CPython 3.14 privatized WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy to

667	        # name is gone so this keeps working on 3.12-3.14. Reading the
668	        # removed public name can raise NameError (not AttributeError) via
669	        # asyncio's own deprecation shim, which a bare getattr(..., default)
670	        # would NOT catch — a plain try/except is used instead, and a
671	        # missing private name too fails with the clear RuntimeError below
672	        # rather than an obscure AttributeError/NameError.
673	        try:
674	            # mypy's python_version=3.14 target sheds the public name from
675	            # typeshed entirely (see pyproject.toml's [tool.mypy]) — this is
676	            # exactly the removed-on-3.14 case the except branch below handles
677	            # at runtime; ignore is scoped to this one attribute reference.
678	            selector_policy_cls = asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
679	        except (AttributeError, NameError):
680	            selector_policy_cls = getattr(asyncio, "_WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy", None)
681	        if selector_policy_cls is None:
682	            raise RuntimeError(
683	                "mcpg: this Python's asyncio module exposes neither WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy "
684	                "nor _WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy; the Windows selector-loop policy mcpg needs for "
685	                "psycopg can't be set. Please file a bug with your Python version."
686	            )

690	    # large, overloaded ``uvicorn.run`` signature; the dict's contents
691	    # are already constrained by ``_uvicorn_tls_kwargs``.
692	    uvicorn.run(app, host=settings.http_host, port=settings.http_port, **tls_kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

51	        self._lock: asyncio.Lock | None = None

54	        """Attempt to consume 1 token. Returns True if allowed, False if throttled."""
55	        if self._lock is None:
56	            self._lock = asyncio.Lock()
57	
58	        if not self.enabled:
59	            return True
60	
61	        # Fall back to "global" if current_role is not active/configured
62	        client_id = current_role.get() or "global"
63	        is_heavy = tool_name in HEAVY_TOOLS
64	
65	        max_tokens = self.heavy_max if is_heavy else self.global_max
66	        window = self.heavy_window if is_heavy else self.global_window
67	
68	        if max_tokens <= 0 or window <= 0:
69	            return True
70	
71	        fill_rate = max_tokens / window
72	        now = time.monotonic()
73	        key = (client_id, is_heavy)
74	
75	        async with self._lock:
76	            bucket = self._buckets.get(key)
77	            if bucket is None:
78	                # Initialize fully loaded bucket
79	                bucket = TokenBucket(tokens=float(max_tokens), last_update=now)
80	                self._buckets[key] = bucket
81	            else:
82	                # Refill tokens based on elapsed time
83	                elapsed = now - bucket.last_update
84	                refill = elapsed * fill_rate
85	                bucket.tokens = min(float(max_tokens), bucket.tokens + refill)
86	                bucket.last_update = now
